assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 closed the Standard Model and confirmed, with a clear clue from nature, a mechanism proposed in 1964. The 2013 prize honoured the theory; the observation itself, a decades-long instrumental and analytical achievement, has not been recognised. Importance, clarity and lasting impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The decisive experimental credit is collective (ATLAS and CMS), so the fair configuration is the three credited founders and long-term leaders of the proposals and detectors. Whether the statutes and committee tradition can honour project leadership over thousands of colleagues, and whether this reflects the decisive individual contributions, is a real allocation problem I cannot resolve from the longlist alone.
assessment.maturity: Two independent experiments, thirteen years of Run 1-3 measurements of couplings and spin-parity; the interpretation is very stable. Recognition is now timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit makes any three-person selection contestable.
Whether other individuals, such as spokespersons or key analysts, deserve credit is not settled by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos by IceCube opened neutrino astronomy and gave a new messenger for the extreme universe, with the later association of a flare with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic-plane detection. It is a discovery found in nature, with existential and cosmic-ray-origin implications.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA, so he is the clearest single credited name. A larger configuration would need other names not in this entry; I therefore propose only him, noting that the list gives a single-person credit for a large collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established at high significance, the source associations are partial and still developing, and the origin of most events remains open. Substantial but maturing.
uncertainties: Source identification is incomplete; only a few associations are established.
Single-name credit for a big collaboration may be seen as incomplete by colleagues and external experts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray (BeppoSAX) and optical/radio afterglow detections of gamma-ray bursts settled the long-standing distance question, proving cosmological origin and linking long bursts to collapsing massive stars. This is a clean discovery driven by observation, with lasting consequences for high-energy astrophysics and cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of the X-ray afterglow in 1997, while Kulkarni's group secured the optical/radio counterpart and redshift for the decisive extragalactic picture. This is a plausible three-person split, though other optical teams (e.g. van Paradijs, Djorgovski) may claim credit and I cannot verify the priority sequence independently.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed over nearly three decades by Swift, Fermi and multiwavelength follow-up, including the GRB-supernova link. Mature, and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Competing credit for the first optical afterglow and redshift measurement.
Compound discovery: X-ray localisation and optical identification may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators and its prompt experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells opened a major field of condensed matter physics, connecting topology to materials and transport.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theoretical foundation; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental confirmation (with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposing HgTe, who are not in this entry). The three-name split is reasonable, but the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the 3D topological insulator experiments (Hasan, Cava and others) complicate fairness.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation by many groups, and the field has matured for nearly twenty years. Timely.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit for the HgTe proposal and the 3D topological insulator discovery.
Practical impact is still mostly conceptual and may rank below discoveries in nature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's all-sky microwave maps gave precision measurements of the age, geometry and composition of the universe and established the standard LambdaCDM model with striking clarity. The lasting impact on cosmology is very large.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a principal instrument and measurement scientist, and Spergel was central in the cosmological interpretation. A reasonable configuration, though collaboration-scale credit and prior COBE, Planck and cosmology prizes make allocation less clean.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and superseded in precision by Planck; mature, but the Committee has already recognised CMB work (2006) and cosmological parameters (2011, 2019), so the marginal novelty is lower.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier CMB and dark-energy prizes.
Planck and other teams may be seen as equally deserving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength idea, reached uncertainties near 10^-18, and has opened precision tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a potential redefinition of the second. Original and clearly stated.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye developed the clocks to the highest precision and with the frequency comb link. A clean two-person claim; other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Hollberg) may deserve mention and I cannot verify all priorities.
assessment.maturity: Several independent clocks agree at the 10^-18 level; the redefinition of the second is still pending, so practical culmination is slightly premature but science is solid.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes on frequency combs and ion clocks.
Redefinition of the second has not yet taken place.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the 2018 discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states launched moire quantum materials, a large and original field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. A natural theory-plus-experiment configuration, though the Cao et al. first-author role and other experiments (e.g. Dean, Young, Yankowitz) feed into the story.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced, but the mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet stable and recognition might be premature.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unresolved.
Allocation among theorists and experimentalists is not obviously settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Gauge/gravity duality is a profound theoretical insight with a huge influence on quantum gravity, black-hole physics and strongly coupled systems. As a string theorist I know its power, yet I place it low for a physics prize because it lacks a direct confirmation in nature.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena's 1997 conjecture is the origin, while Witten and Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov made it computationally precise. The credited list omits Gubser and Klebanov, so a Polyakov-Witten-Maldacena configuration is imperfect and disputed.
assessment.maturity: Enormous internal consistency checks and numerous applications, but no empirical test of the quantum-gravity claim; recognition would be premature for a prize that insists on clues from nature.
uncertainties: No direct observational confirmation of the duality as a statement about our universe.
Attribution disputes; the real-world relevance of QCD-like applications is approximate.
